Hi Alice / Tessa — adding technical detail for the addendum draft. Below is suggested legal- and procurement-ready SLO wording plus an operational fallback playbook. Please review and tell us where you'd like tougher or looser guarantees.

Suggested SLO language (high level):
- Reserved Pool Throughput Commitment: Redwood will provision a dedicated pool that provides a sustained throughput of 45,000 tokens/sec measured as the 95th percentile of 1-hour rolling windows over each calendar day. The pool will allow bursts up to 60,000 tokens/sec for sliding windows not exceeding 5 minutes, subject to available capacity and KV cache warming.

- Latency Objective: For the sustained throughput periods, a 99th percentile per-token latency of <= 180ms (measured at Redwood ingress) is targeted when using the designated model family. Latency SLO excludes customer-side network variance and models that differ from the certified model variants attached.

- Measurement & Reporting:
  * Metrics source: Redwood telemetry (ingress QPS, tokens/sec measured at service boundary, per-request token counts).
  * Reporting cadence: daily aggregates and a monthly SLO report showing breaches, root cause analysis, and mitigation actions.

- Remediation (service credits):
  * Single-day breach of sustained throughput (95th %ile 1h windows < 45k): 5% service credit of monthly Dedicated fee.
  * Two or more days in a 30-day period: 15% credit.
  * Material breach (sustained below 30k tokens/sec for > 6 consecutive hours): 40% credit and joint incident review.

- Fallback policy (operational playbook):
  1) Auto-scale attempt: Redwood will attempt to expand the dedicated pool within the customer's burst policy (up to negotiated burst GPUs) within 10 minutes.
  2) If capacity cannot be added within 30 minutes, requests will be routed to a warmed, compatible hosted model variant with a documented latency/cost delta. Redwood will preserve customer prefixes and KV cache best-effort; a warning banner will be emitted in the console and a notification to the customer's on-call will be sent.
  3) If routed to hosted fallback, Redwood will apply the customer's reserved pricing for within-quota usage for the duration of the fallback window up to 6 hours; beyond that, standard hosted overage pricing applies unless otherwise agreed.

- Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance windows (>=72h notice) and force majeure events are excluded from SLO calculations. Customer misconfiguration (malformed prompts, excessive parallelism beyond agreed concurrency) may result in reduced effective throughput and is subject to analysis as non-redwood-caused.

Operational notes: KV cache warm-up can reduce observed tokens/sec for the first ~10 minutes after a large traffic pattern change; we recommend a 15-minute buffer during big launches and can add a temporary pre-warm run prior to promotions.

I'm attaching a CSV with recent load tests we ran that demonstrate 48k sustained with 8 GPUs when using our recommendations (quantization + batching profile). We can tighten credit formulas if procurement pushes back.

—Vivek
